record.paper_title: A Few Problems on Monodromy and Discriminants
record.context_brief: sufficiency of parabolic-point and cuspidal-edge obstructions
record.original_question: In odd dimension n, non-degenerate parabolic points of the complexification of the boundary, and generic cuspidal edges occurring instead of such parabolic points, obstruct algebraicity of the hyperplane cut-volume function. Are these geometric obstructions sufficient to solve Arnold's problem: must the complexification of every smooth algebraic boundary of degree at least 3 of a compact domain in R^n have a point of one of these obstructing types? If not, can the obstruction list be completed by other singularity types whose occurrence is unavoidable and which also obstruct algebraicity?

evidence.quote:
Proposition (see [15]). If n is odd and the volume function deﬁned by
a bounded domain with smooth boundary in Rn is algebraic, then the
complexiﬁcation of this boundary cannot have non-degenera te parabolic
points in Cn.

However, the standard singular points which can occur instead of
parabolic points, the generic cuspidal edges , also prevent the algebraic-
ity of the corresponding volume function, see [15], §III.6.

Problem 4. Are these geometric obstructions suﬃcient to solve the
above problem?
(That is, is it correct that the complexiﬁcation of the smooth alge-
braic boundary of degree ≥ 3 of a compact domain in Rn always has a
point of one of these two obstructing types?) If not, probably we can
complete this list by some other singularity types, also obstructing t he
algebraicity, in such a way that singular points of at least one of thes e
types will be unavoidable on any such hypersurface?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a compact domain with smooth algebraic boundary $\Sigma$ of degree $\geq 3$, and assume $n$ is odd. For a generic affine hyperplane $H \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, define the cut-volume function $V(H)$ to be the $n$-dimensional volume of one of the two parts into which $H$ divides $D$, considered as a (multivalued) function on the space of affine hyperplanes.

A point $p$ of the complexification $\Sigma_{\mathbb{C}} \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ is called a non-degenerate parabolic point if the second fundamental form of $\Sigma_{\mathbb{C}}$ at $p$ is degenerate but its kernel is one-dimensional and transverse, in the standard non-degeneracy sense. A generic cuspidal edge is the standard codimension-one singularity that may occur on $\Sigma_{\mathbb{C}}$ in place of a parabolic point.

It is known that, in odd dimension $n$, if $V$ is algebraic then $\Sigma_{\mathbb{C}}$ has neither non-degenerate parabolic points nor generic cuspidal edges.

Question (two parts):

(a) Is it true that for every compact domain $D \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n$ odd) with smooth algebraic boundary $\Sigma$ of degree $\geq 3$, the complexification $\Sigma_{\mathbb{C}}$ must contain at least one non-degenerate parabolic point or at least one generic cuspidal edge?

(b) If (a) fails, determine an enlarged finite list $\mathcal{L}$ of singularity types — each type obstructing algebraicity of $V$ — such that for every such $\Sigma$ the complexification $\Sigma_{\mathbb{C}}$ unavoidably contains a singularity of some type in $\mathcal{L}$.
artifact.category_tag: algebraicity of volume functions and singularities of algebraic hypersurfaces
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this problem was found. It is posed as an open problem in the context of Arnold's question on algebraicity of the cut-volume function for smooth algebraic boundaries in odd-dimensional Euclidean space, and searches return no announcement of a proof or counterexample for either part (a) or (b).
